decisions.reason: The vertigo combination tablet sits close to the firm's core prescription offer, has its own product page, and pharmaceutical approvals are costly to obtain, so withdrawing it one year after launch is unlikely.

The generic antidepressant is distant from the firm's established offer and exposed to price pressure from reimbursement tenders, but it is newly approved and has its own page, so the firm will likely keep it for now.
The combination antihypertensive matches the firm's competence in improved, adherence-friendly formulations and is close to its core range, making a drop unlikely.
The supplement fits the strategy of building pharmacy-exclusive self-care products, but its weaker web presence and the low cost of exiting supplements give it a somewhat higher drop risk.
